name: Methyprylon
summary: Sedative of the pipeidinedone family. The drug was used for treating insomnia, but is rarely used today due to alternatives with fewer side effects, such as benzodiazepines.

uses.text: Methyprylon, ormethyprylone is a piperidinedione derivative and CNS depressant drug marketed by Hoffmann-La Roche in the 1950s, marketed under the trade name Noludar and advertised as treatment of insomnia as a nonbarbiturate. According to the Encyclopedia of Toxicology (2005), methyprylon was withdrawn from the United States market in 1988.

sideEffects.text: Despite early reports describing methyprylon as an effective hypnotic, concerns regarding intoxication and dependence became increasingly apparent during the following decade. Reports of overdose, suicide attempts, and dependence contributed to a changing assessment of its safety profile. Reports of serious intoxication began appearing in the medical literature as early as 1956.
